newsitem.title: USA: Kentucky's Sen. Ford to retire, aide says.
newsitem.headline: Kentucky's Sen. Ford to retire, aide says.

text.p: Sen. Wendell Ford of Kentucky, the second ranking Democrat in the Senate, will not seek re-election next year, a spokesman said Monday.

Ford, 72, was the second senior Democrat in the past three weeks to quit the Senate. His decision could further weaken his party's chances of regaining control of the Senate where Republicans now hold a 55-45 edge.
Ford was to hold a news conference in Kentucky Monday afternoon to announce his decision to leave after four terms in the Senate.
On Feb. 20, Sen. John Glenn of Ohio, 75, announced his retirement, opening the way for a contest in that state where Republicans think they have a good chance of winning his seat.

The political fallout from the Ford decision was less clear since the move caught many by surprise. Representative Jim Bunning, 65, the Hall of Fame baseball player and popular Republican who has served in the House since 1986, has been widely reported preparing a run for the Senate.

Potential Democratic candidates include Representative Scotty Baesler, Lt. Gov. Steve Henry and state Attorney General Ben Chandler -- grandson of former Kentucky governor, senator and baseball commissioner "Happy" Chandler. Ford was first elected to the Senate in 1974.
